chapter: Jazz at the Philharmonic and the record business
title: Prejudice in California, Dexter Gordon and a white wife
summary: California police harassed musicians; McGhee left, and recalls girls at Hawkins' opening.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Well, that brings up another point. You were talking about prejudice in the South before, and of course we know there was prejudice in the North, too, but it was more subtle...
...not as out in the open. But California, as you said, it was Country and it was really very Southwestern.
Yeah, Southwestern-Country. That's what it was.
And you did run into some problems there which I think

Yeah, they messed with you. Anybody that don't know what they're doing will be hung... Many a musician... Like Dexter Gordon went back out there, but he didn't know what he was going back into. He thought that because he was Dexter Gordon, he was going to get everything that was coming to him. He got everything that was coming to him, all right. They put him in jail every time he turned around.

That's why I split from out there. I saw what was happening, and I'd say, "Well, gee, I ain't gonna be out here in this mess, playing... Let me get out of here." Because I wasn't doing anything bad, but I mean, what they thought was bad, it would be anything, you know.
Well, you were also married to a White woman.
And that was taboo. Yeah, that was really...
So they were after you for that.

Yeah, they didn't like me for that. But what can you say? You just have to make it. If they don't like you there, split, and go somewhere else! I come here to New York and I ain't had no problems like that, you know. And I've been living with a White woman for as long as I can remember, damn near. Even before... When I was with Andy,
when I first met White girls hanging out, I was cool. You know, we got along good together. I didn't have no animosity towards them.

But boy, they really had it for me out in California, though. And I had all the girls in my... I had five girls that come sit at the table the first night I opened up with Coleman Hawkins out there. They all sat at the table, and all of us there... Me, her...yeah, her...her...her -- five of them. Beautiful girls, too, you know. I said, "Well, now, I'll just stay away here!" I didn't want the world to know what I was doing, you know. So I said to them, "Cool it. I'll get back to you. I'll get to you when you want to (?)." But you can't go along with that.
